claims.label: Terrell accessed an SD card on his laptop at the crime scene
claims.claim: Terrell Farnsworth inserted an SD card into his laptop and worked on it within approximately 10 minutes of Charlie Kirk being shot, as shown in episode footage.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the original raw footage and forensic metadata to confirm SD-card insertion sequence; cross-reference with David Hull testimony on chain of custody.

claims.label: Terrell showed laptop content to Philip Goldsbury shortly after the shooting
claims.claim: Episode footage shows Terrell Farnsworth displaying content on his laptop screen to Philip Goldsbury approximately 10 minutes after Charlie Kirk's death.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify and interview Philip Goldsbury regarding the content shown; obtain his contemporaneous account.

claims.label: Terrell never provided the original SD card to investigators
claims.claim: Per David Hull's preliminary-hearing testimony referenced by Ana Kasparian, Terrell Farnsworth did not turn over the physical SD card to investigators; only Google links and a flash drive were provided.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm SD-card disposition against official evidence logs; subpoena physical media if it exists.

claims.label: David Hull testified investigators did not receive the SD cards
claims.claim: Lead investigator David Hull testified at the preliminary hearing that he did not receive the physical SD cards taken from the scene.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the preliminary-hearing transcript and confirm testimony verbatim.

claims.label: Mark Bricker testified the Utah County Attorney's Office created the 20-minute sizzle reel
claims.claim: SBI Sergeant Mark Bricker testified at the preliminary hearing that the Utah County Attorney's Office — not the court — created the 20-minute sizzle reel shown in court.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Bricker's full preliminary-hearing testimony; request the prosecution's production logs and version history for the sizzle reel.

claims.label: The 20-minute sizzle reel has a decreased (modified) aspect ratio
claims.claim: The aspect ratio of the 20-minute sizzle reel shown at the preliminary hearing was decreased relative to the source footage, as demonstrated in the episode by normal-speed and slow-motion display.
claims.investigative_direction: Have a forensic video analyst compare the sizzle reel against raw UVU surveillance footage to quantify the aspect-ratio shift.

claims.label: Anonymous federal-court employee stated federal courts do not alter video evidence
claims.claim: Per an email from an anonymous federal-court employee read on air, video and photo evidence is never altered in any federal court the employee has worked in, because alteration would prejudice the jury.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the email's authenticity through metadata; corroborate with court policy documentation. Treat as anonymous-source claim pending verification.

claims.label: Host presents the decreased aspect ratio as the prosecution's doing, not the court's
claims.claim: The host asserts that the entity which decreased the aspect ratio was the prosecution (Utah County Attorney's Office), the FBI, or another party — but not the court itself.
claims.investigative_direction: Trace the production chain of the sizzle reel through prosecution discovery logs; identify all parties with custody between raw footage and exhibit.

claims.label: Andrew Kolvet claimed Candace conceded the debate
claims.claim: On the Kolvet/Neff podcast, Andrew Kolvet stated that Candace conceded the debate early and repeatedly and predicted the loss would "age well" for him.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare this characterization to a transcript of the debate Candace participated in; identify specific concessions alleged.

claims.label: Andrew Wilson defended Candace on the Hitler-clip interpretation
claims.claim: On the Kolvet/Neff podcast, Andrew Wilson stated that after reviewing the clip he concluded Candace was making a nationalism comparison rather than apologizing for Hitler, and pushed back on Blake Neff's framing.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate the original Candace clip being referenced; transcribe the full segment in context.

claims.label: Charlie Kirk stated in November 2023 that Candace is "on our team"
claims.claim: A November 2023 clip of Charlie Kirk shows him saying Candace is "on our team" and telling a critic asking about her AmFest appearance to "lose my number."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the full unedited segment; note any surrounding context that may complicate the read.

claims.label: Andrew Kolvet briefed Candace on Bill Aman summit, BB Netanyahu letter, and Charlie's texts to Dan Flood
claims.claim: Text messages and calls between Candace and Andrew Kolvet from September 11–14, 2025 show Kolvet briefing Candace on the Bill Aman summit, the BB Netanyahu letter, and Charlie Kirk's text messages to Dan Flood the night before.
claims.investigative_direction: Preserve the original text-message exports with metadata; obtain contemporaneous corroboration from other TPUSA insiders if available.

claims.label: Kolvet told Candace on September 14, 2025 that the TPUSA board had voted in Erica Kirk
claims.claim: Per text/call artifacts, Andrew Kolvet told Candace on September 14, 2025 that the TPUSA board had already voted in Erica Kirk to take over the organization, and asked her not to announce it yet.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference with TPUSA corporate filings, board minutes, and Erica Kirk's public statements around the leadership transition.
